description: A color's invoiced amount is the number of invoice line items for products of that color.

b.request: Count invoice line items for each product color, treating products with no color as a separate group; calculate each color’s count as a share of all invoice line items, keep colors whose count exceeds the average count per color, and return one row containing their average count, average share, and average amount above that per-color average, without rounding
b.sql: WITH color_counts AS (SELECT p.product_color, COUNT(*) AS item_count FROM Invoice_Line_Items AS ili JOIN Products AS p ON p.product_id = ili.product_id GROUP BY p.product_color), color_stats AS (SELECT item_count, 1.0 * item_count / SUM(item_count) OVER () AS item_share, AVG(1.0 * item_count) OVER () AS average_count_per_color FROM color_counts) SELECT AVG(item_count) AS average_count, AVG(item_share) AS average_share, AVG(item_count - average_count_per_color) AS average_amount_above_per_color_average FROM color_stats WHERE item_count > average_count_per_color

c.request: How much of each product color was invoiced? Products with no color count as their own group. Work out each color's share of the total invoiced. Look at the colors whose invoiced amount is above the average per color. For those colors, give one row with their average invoiced amount, their average share, and how far above the per-color average they are on average. Don't round anything. A color's invoiced amount is the number of invoice line items for products of that color.
c.sql: WITH color_amounts AS (SELECT p.product_color, COUNT(ili.order_item_id) AS invoiced_amount FROM Products AS p LEFT JOIN Invoice_Line_Items AS ili ON ili.product_id = p.product_id GROUP BY p.product_color), per_color AS (SELECT invoiced_amount, 1.0 * invoiced_amount / NULLIF(SUM(invoiced_amount) OVER (), 0) AS share, AVG(1.0 * invoiced_amount) OVER () AS average_per_color FROM color_amounts) SELECT AVG(1.0 * invoiced_amount) AS average_invoiced_amount, AVG(share) AS average_share, AVG(invoiced_amount - average_per_color) AS average_amount_above_per_color_average FROM per_color WHERE invoiced_amount > average_per_color;

a.request: For each product color, count how many invoice line items were for products of that color. Products with no color count as their own group. Work out each color's share of the overall number of line items. Keep the colors whose count is above the average count per color. Over those colors, give one row with the average count, the average share, and the average amount by which the count exceeds the per-color average. Don't round anything.
a.sql: WITH color_counts AS (SELECT p.product_color, COUNT(*) AS line_item_count FROM Invoice_Line_Items AS ili JOIN Products AS p ON p.product_id = ili.product_id GROUP BY p.product_color), color_stats AS (SELECT product_color, line_item_count, 1.0 * line_item_count / SUM(line_item_count) OVER () AS share, AVG(line_item_count) OVER () AS average_per_color FROM color_counts) SELECT AVG(line_item_count) AS average_count, AVG(share) AS average_share, AVG(line_item_count - average_per_color) AS average_excess FROM color_stats WHERE line_item_count > average_per_color

d.request: How many invoice line items are there for products of each color, treating products with no color as their own group? Calculate each color’s share of the total line items. For colors whose line item count exceeds the average count per color, return one row showing their average line item count, average share, and average amount above the per-color average. Do not round any values.
d.sql: WITH color_counts AS (SELECT p.product_color, COUNT(*) AS line_item_count FROM Invoice_Line_Items AS ili JOIN Products AS p ON p.product_id = ili.product_id GROUP BY p.product_color), totals AS (SELECT AVG(line_item_count) AS average_count_per_color, SUM(line_item_count) AS total_line_items FROM color_counts) SELECT AVG(c.line_item_count) AS average_line_item_count, AVG(1.0 * c.line_item_count / t.total_line_items) AS average_share, AVG(c.line_item_count - t.average_count_per_color) AS average_amount_above_per_color_average FROM color_counts AS c CROSS JOIN totals AS t WHERE c.line_item_count > t.average_count_per_color;
